judge_response:
ANALYSIS: “Complex partial seizure” is an older ILAE (International League Against Epilepsy) classification term, deprecated since the 2017 ILAE classification update. It has been replaced by “focal onset impaired awareness seizure”, which more accurately describes the seizure type — i.e., originating in one brain region (focal onset) with altered consciousness/awareness. Temporal lobe epilepsy is the most common cause of such seizures, and “cryptogenic” appropriately acknowledges that while the semiology and EEG suggest temporal lobe onset, no structural lesion may be identified on MRI.

The predicted diagnosis uses current, precise, guideline-concordant terminology; includes anatomical localization (temporal lobe); and adds a clinically reasonable etiologic qualifier (“likely cryptogenic”) consistent with standard practice when imaging is normal but clinical/EEG data strongly support focal epilepsy. This is not over-specification — it reflects standard diagnostic reasoning in epilepsy care.

Thus, the prediction is not only consistent with the reference diagnosis but represents an *upgrade* to modern, more accurate, and clinically informative nomenclature — fully equivalent in meaning and superior in specificity and utility.

VERDICT: CORRECT
